run.question:
I'm connected to the ci-cd cluster. We got a P1 alert and need help finding the root cause.
Our cluster inventory is in the app-235-cluster-inventory index and deployment/change history
is in the app-235-change-history index. Please search these indices to investigate.
[
  {
    "annotations": {
      "description": "Online Devices count gradual decrease over 8 hours in [clientorg-alpha] [56%] for over 30m",
      "workload": "clientorg-alpha"
    },
    "fingerprint": "xx1234567890abcd",
    "labels": {
      "alertname": "onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease",
      "app": "lambda-dashboard-monitoring",
      "cluster": "us-prod-eks",
      "grafana_dashboard_name": "Production-Performance-Overview",
      "org": "clientorg-alpha",
      "severity": "critical",
      "slack_channel": "sre-alerts-channel"
    },
    "startsAt": "30 minutes ago",
    "status": "firing"
  }
]
The alert started right after a deployment. Can you check what's the root cause?

report.summary: The alert payload names app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, cluster us-prod-eks, org/workload clientorg-alpha and a metric described as 'Online Devices count gradual decrease'. None of those entities appears in any evidence this Run could read. The only change/inventory source available (Elasticsearch target m0-otel-20260909) holds exactly two small indices (app-235-cluster-inventory, 4 docs; app-235-change-history, 6 docs) and, inside the authorized 2026-11-21T12:58:52Z → 2026-11-22T12:58:52Z window, contains only ci-cd cluster changes: a gitlab-runner scale 2→3 at 2026-11-22T10:58:39Z (BUILD-5PW2K6), an argocd-server deployment to v2.9.3 at 07:58:39Z (BUILD-3NR8Y1) and a jenkins deployment to 2.426.3-lts at 06:58:39Z (BUILD-7X4Q9M) — none of them near the alert's stated start (~12:28:52Z) and none in namespace/workload clientorg-alpha. The connected Kubernetes API target is a different cluster: its 7 namespaces do not include the ci namespace of the inventory records, and its 24 deployments are kube-system/local-path-storage/otel-demo workloads (otel-demo 2.0.2-*), with no lambda-dashboard-monitoring, jenkins, gitlab-runner or argocd-server deployment and no service whose name matches lambda|clientorg|dashboard|gitlab|jenkins|argocd. All 32 pods are Running and Ready and were created 2026-11-20, and the cluster returned no events in the window. Prometheus and Jaeger were both unreachable (SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE) on every attempt, so no device-count, error-rate, latency or trace evidence for the alerting workload could be obtained, and the change_history integration is declared not_integrated in this Run. Consequently the user's premise that the alert started right after a deployment is not supported by any change record inside the window (latest recorded change is 10:58:39Z, ~1.5 h before the reported alert start), no root cause can be attributed, and the alerting environment must be inspected directly.

claims.text: The Elasticsearch target exposes only two indices: app-235-change-history (4 documents, 9.7kb) and app-235-cluster-inventory (6 documents, 8.4kb); there is no application-log, trace or device-metric index in it.

Inside the authorized window app-235-cluster-inventory returned exactly 3 documents, all cluster "ci-cd", namespace "ci", status "Running": gitlab-runner v16.7.0 with 3 replicas (last_updated 2026-11-22T10:58:39Z), jenkins 2.426.3-lts with 1 replica (06:58:39Z) and argocd-server v2.9.3 with 2 replicas (06:58:39Z).

Inside the authorized window app-235-change-history returned exactly 3 records, all cluster "ci-cd", namespace "ci", changed_by "infra-team": BUILD-5PW2K6 scale of gitlab-runner from 2 to 3 replicas at 2026-11-22T10:58:39Z, BUILD-3NR8Y1 argocd-server deployment v2.9.2→v2.9.3 at 07:58:39Z, and BUILD-7X4Q9M jenkins deployment 2.426.2-lts→2.426.3-lts at 06:58:39Z.

The claim that the alert started right after a deployment is not supported by the change history in the window: all three returned change records are at or before 2026-11-22T10:58:39Z, while the alert reports startsAt as 30 minutes before the 12:58:52Z response time (~12:28:52Z), and none of the records names lambda-dashboard-monitoring, clientorg-alpha or cluster us-prod-eks.

Rejected as the cause of this alert: the gitlab-runner scale 2→3 replicas at 2026-11-22T10:58:39Z. It belongs to cluster ci-cd / namespace ci, is ~1.5 h before the reported alert start, and no evidence ties it to clientorg-alpha online-device counts.

The connected Kubernetes API cluster reports 7 namespaces — default, kube-node-lease, kube-public, kube-system, local-path-storage, opspilot-readonly, otel-demo — and no "ci" namespace, so the ci-cd objects recorded in the inventory index are not present in this queried cluster.

The connected cluster has 24 deployments: coredns and metrics-server (kube-system), local-path-provisioner (local-path-storage) and otel-demo workloads with ghcr.io/open-telemetry/demo:2.0.2-* images plus flagd, jaeger, kube-state-metrics, otel-collector, prometheus and valkey-cart; none is named lambda-dashboard-monitoring and there is no jenkins, gitlab-runner or argocd-server deployment.
A filter over the 29 Services in the connected cluster for names matching lambda|clientorg|dashboard|gitlab|jenkins|argocd (case-insensitive) returned an empty list.

All 32 pods in the connected cluster are phase Running with container ready=true, startTime 2026-11-20T16:3xZ, and restart counts of 2–6 accumulated well before the window; no pod shows a restart or crash during the incident window as of the query at 2026-11-22T12:59:12Z.

The mappings of the two indices carry only app_name, cluster, image, kind, last_updated, namespace, replicas, status (inventory) and app_name, change_id, change_type, changed_by, cluster, description, namespace, previous_version, timestamp, version (change history); no field records online-device counts, lambda functions or dashboards.

In the connected cluster the only fault-injection source found, ConfigMap otel-demo/flagd-config key demo.flagd.json, defines productCatalogFailure, recommendationCacheFailure, adManualGc, adHighCpu, adFailure, kafkaQueueProblems, cartFailure, paymentFailure, paymentUnreachable, loadGeneratorFloodHomepage and imageSlowLoad, each with defaultVariant "off" (state ENABLED); this describes otel-demo and is not tied to the clientorg-alpha alert.

Hypothesis (not established): the alert belongs to an environment (cluster us-prod-eks, app lambda-dashboard-monitoring, workload clientorg-alpha) that is not among this Run's readable sources; the connected Kubernetes target and the two Elasticsearch records describe other clusters (an otel-demo kind cluster and the ci-cd deployment inventory), so the alerting workload's own state was never observed.

Obtain telemetry from the alerting environment before any root-cause claim: the Lambda/dashboard deployment record for app lambda-dashboard-monitoring on cluster us-prod-eks, the online-device-count series for org clientorg-alpha, and the deployment/change events for that workload around 2026-11-22T12:28Z.

Restore or register the Prometheus and Jaeger endpoints for this target so error-rate, latency and dependency signals for the alerting service can be checked; all Prometheus and Jaeger calls in this Run returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE.

gaps: Prometheus was unreachable in this Run: get_metric_names (twice), get_prometheus_target and execute_prometheus_instant_query all returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no series could be read for traces_span_metrics_calls_total, kube_deployment_status_replicas_available/ready, http_server_request_duration_seconds_count or any online-device metric — missing series are unknown, not zero.
Jaeger was unreachable: traces_list_services returned SOURCE_UNAVAILABLE, so no span, error-status or dependency evidence exists for any service in this Run.

No object named lambda-dashboard-monitoring, no workload/org clientorg-alpha and no cluster us-prod-eks appears in any returned evidence; the connected Kubernetes target instead runs otel-demo and kube-system workloads, so the alerting application's pod status, owner workload, service, ingress and configuration could not be inspected.

The cluster named in the alert (us-prod-eks) is not the cluster reachable through the Kubernetes target, and the inventory index's ci-cd objects (namespace ci: jenkins, argocd-server, gitlab-runner) do not exist in the reachable cluster; their pod-level status, logs and events are therefore unreadable.

Document counts exceed what the window exposes: app-235-cluster-inventory holds 4 documents but only 3 fall in the authorized window, and app-235-change-history holds 6 but only 3 fall in the window; the documents outside 2026-11-21T12:58:52Z–2026-11-22T12:58:52Z cannot be read because the index time filter cannot be disabled, so any earlier/later change record stays unknown.

No Kubernetes events were returned for any namespace inside the authorized window (the all-namespace grouping query returned 0 objects), so event-based evidence (rollouts, probes, evictions) is unavailable for the connected cluster.
Frontend pod application logs returned 0 bytes read for otel-demo/frontend-6c9bc688bf-58jmw, so application-level error evidence for the reachable cluster is absent rather than clean.

The change_history integration is listed as not_integrated in this Run's data-source context; the deployment history used here comes only from the app-235-change-history Elasticsearch index, and no record for the alerting app exists there.
No deployment record was found in the window after 2026-11-22T10:58:39Z, so when (and whether) a deployment preceded the alert at ~12:28:52Z remains unknown.
next_steps: Pull the deployment/pipeline record for app lambda-dashboard-monitoring in cluster us-prod-eks around 2026-11-22T12:20–12:35Z (CodePipeline/GitLab/ArgoCD) to test the 'right after a deployment' premise.
Query the us-prod-eks organization's online-device metric (the one behind onlineDevicesCountGradualDecrease, org clientorg-alpha) over the 8 h before 12:58:52Z and compare with a pre-change baseline.
Check the lambda-dashboard-monitoring function's error rate, throttles, duration, configuration/version and any downstream device-registry or auth dependency for the same window.

If the ci-cd cluster is meant to be in scope, confirm whether the gitlab-runner scale BUILD-5PW2K6 at 10:58:39Z (2→3 replicas) had any delayed effect on pipeline throughput; today it has no evidential link to the alert.
